Final Fantasy VI: Symphonic Poem (Born with the Gift of Magic) by Royal Stockholm Philharmonic Orchestra, arranged by Roger Wanamo

Bravo.

On my first listen, I have to admit I wasn't immensely impressed by it. The execution and quality is top notch professional, yes, but the arrangement itself sounded like a mish-mash of familiar melodies. There were some interesting parts though and it is being called a symphonic poem - not just a medley, so I gave it a 2nd and 3rd listen and so on and so forth and now can say that I appreciate it a lot more.

The following is my amateur analysis of the song. First, the timeline/structure of the song:

Opening: Opera theme

0:35: Terra’s theme in the background

1:15 Gestahl Empire theme

2:45 More of Terra’s theme and Gestahl Empire’s theme

4:00 Kefka’s theme

7:40 Esper World interspersed with Terra’s theme

9:20 Music box Terra theme

10:40 Kefka’s theme in the background

Frantic fight/battle themes:

10:50 Metamorphosis, 11:20 The Unforgiven, 11:50 Battle theme

13:15 Save Them theme with Kefka’s theme

13:35 Slow part of Dancing Mad theme

15:10 Terra’s theme

17:30 Back to Opera theme

The song opens and closes with themes from the opera. No coincidence here. The composer is presenting his "take" on FF6 as a story or symphonic poem. Just like the opera in FF6 is some playwright's story about Draco and Maria, this is the composer Wanamo's story about the FF6 epic. It's apt to reference the opera when you want to present a story in an "FF6 way."

The next sections are Terra's theme and Gestahl Empire's theme going back and forth. TBH, this is sort of expected in any grand arrangement of FF6 since the story of the game itself does this in its beginning.

Next, Kefka's theme. The composer must have really liked this theme because he devotes almost 4 minutes to it, hehe.

The next section is the Esper World theme intertwined with Terra's theme. This section IMHO was amazing and bar none my favorite part of the song. The Esper World theme arranged for orchestra here is perfect. Spooky, ethereal, mysterious, YET not too mysterious because we keep hearing Terra's theme. (The game's original Esper World track is a lot more in-your-face and threatening... almost too much, since espers aren't bad creatures or anything.) I highlighted the music box version of Terra's theme because I believe this is the composer referencing Terra's birth during that whole flashback we see in the game that tells the story of Terra's parents and her birth. That was excellent. The music box version of Terra tells of Terra's birth and infancy in the Esper World.

Next, Kefka's theme comes back and then a succession of frantic, battle themes. Clearly referencing the Empire's assault and raid of the Esper World.

Then, the Save Them theme with Kefka's theme, and then a slow theme from Dancing Mad. The Save Theme is heroic and optimistic and I think tells of a victorious end of the preceding battles of the forces of good over the bad and Kefka. (Again, this is Wanamo's symphonic poem of FF6, not an exact retelling of the flashback we see in the game, so he has the freedom to tell his own FF6 story.) The slow theme from Dancing Mad is Kefka's demise (... or is it not?).

Back to Terra's theme. "Born with the Gift of Magic" is obviously referring to Terra, so no wonder it's the main theme of the song. Also, Born. Another piece of evidence that the music box section is Terra's birth.

And finally, close again with an Opera theme.

Because it's a symphonic poem (supposed to tell a story), I urge people not to listen to this as just another FF6 medley that fortunately happens to be more professional and high-faluting than usual. The composer's choice of melodies was very deliberate, and he succeeds in telling his story of FF6. Bravo.
